reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that scheduling discrepancies—particularly the disproportionate number of times visitors play immediately after games—introduce systematic fatigue effects that distort traditional performance metrics. These effects are modeled using factorial linear and generalized linear models, where variables such as home/visitor status and prior-day play are included. The key mathematical duality lies between raw performance and adjusted performance, where the latter accounts for fatigue and scheduling bias. Failure modes include ignoring overtime effects or assuming independence of team performance across games. The derived kernel of scheduling discrepancy is captured in the difference in frequency of play between home and visiting teams, which directly impacts expected margins of victory. This leads to a redefinition of home court advantage as a residual term after adjustment, revealing it to be negligible under proper modeling.
